student_answer: Artificial Intelligence, or AI, is when computers are programmed to think and make decisions like humans. It helps machines learn from mistakes, recognize human speech, spot trends in data, and handle smart tasks like virtual assistance, recommendation engines, and grading test answers automatically.

Machine Learning is a part of AI where software gets smarter by studying past data instead of being manually programmed with strict rules. The more examples and data you feed into a machine learning model, the better it gets at guessing or calculating the right outputs.

Natural Language Processing (NLP) is how AI systems read and process the language humans speak or write. It's used in tools like Google Translate, chatbots, and grammar checkers. In automatic exam grading, NLP helps check if a student's response matches the meaning of the answer key.

Cloud computing means using online servers to store files, run programs, and host databases instead of keeping everything on your personal hard drive. It makes work accessible from anywhere with an internet connection while saving money on expensive server hardware.

A Database Management System (DBMS) is software that manages large amounts of information neatly and securely. It keeps data organized so it can be queried fast without losing or corrupting important files, which is why banks, schools, and online shops depend on it every day.

Artificial Intelligence refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines. It allows software to process information, adapt to new inputs, solve problems, and execute tasks like language understanding, pattern detection, and automated decision-making without continuous human intervention.

Machine Learning is a subset of AI that focuses on building algorithms that learn from data. Rather than relying on hardcoded instructions, ML algorithms analyze dataset patterns to make data-driven predictions, continuously improving their accuracy as more data becomes available.

Natural Language Processing is a discipline within AI that bridges the gap between human communication and computational understanding.
